---
title: "Multiple-Dose and Steady-State"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, .quiet = TRUE)
```

## Multiple-dose NCA concepts

At steady state, the dosing interval τ (tau) is the key unit of analysis. Instead of analyzing from 0 to ∞, you analyze within one dosing interval [0, τ]. Additional parameters describe how concentrations fluctuate over the interval. Companion chapters complete the steady-state picture: [Automatic Intervals and Dosing Regimens](auto-intervals.qmd) shows the intervals PKNCA generates from the dose times, [Superposition](superposition.qmd) predicts steady-state profiles from single-dose data, [Time to Steady State](tss.qmd) estimates when steady state is reached, and [Secondary Parameters](secondary-parameters.qmd#ratios) computes accumulation ratios.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| τ (tau) | Dosing interval (h) |
| Ctrough | Concentration at end of τ (= concentration at `time = end` of interval) |
| Cmin | Minimum observed concentration within τ |
| Cmax | Peak concentration within τ |
| Cav | Average concentration over τ = AUCτ / τ |
| Peak-trough ratio (PTR) | Cmax / Ctrough |
| Degree of fluctuation | (Cmax − Cmin) / Cav × 100% |
| Swing | (Cmax − Cmin) / Cmin × 100% |

---

## Synthetic steady-state dataset

We simulate steady-state oral theophylline to demonstrate all parameters. The key is that `start` and `end` define a single dosing interval.

```{r}
set.seed(42)

# Theoph-like PK: Ka=1.5/h, ke=0.08/h, V=30L, dose=400mg
ka <- 1.5; ke <- 0.08; V <- 30; dose <- 400; tau <- 12

# One-compartment oral steady-state: C(t) = [dose/V * ka/(ka-ke)] * [e^(-ke*t)/(1-e^(-ke*tau)) - e^(-ka*t)/(1-e^(-ka*tau))]
C_ss <- function(t, ka, ke, V, dose, tau) {
  A <- (dose / V) * (ka / (ka - ke))
  A * (exp(-ke * t) / (1 - exp(-ke * tau)) - exp(-ka * t) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}

timepoints <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)
n_subjects <- 4

d_conc_ss <- expand.grid(Subject = factor(1:n_subjects), time = timepoints) |>
  mutate(
    # Add ~20% log-normal inter-individual variability (IIV) on the elimination rate constant (ke)
    ke_i  = ke * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.2)),
    conc  = mapply(C_ss, time, ka, ke_i, V, dose, tau) + rnorm(n(), 0, 0.05),
    conc  = pmax(conc, 0)
  ) |>
  select(Subject, time, conc)

d_dose_ss <- data.frame(
  Subject = factor(1:n_subjects),
  dose    = dose,
  time    = 0,
  route   = "extravascular"
)

ggplot(d_conc_ss, aes(x = time, y = conc, group = Subject, colour = Subject)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Simulated steady-state oral profiles (one dosing interval)",
       x = "Time within interval (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

---

## Basic steady-state NCA

For a single dosing interval, set `end = tau`. Parameters like `cav`, `ctrough`, `ptr`, `deg.fluc`, and `swing` all require a finite interval end.

```{r}
o_conc_ss <- PKNCAconc(d_conc_ss, conc ~ time | Subject)
o_dose_ss <- PKNCAdose(d_dose_ss, dose ~ time | Subject, route = "extravascular")

ss_intervals <- data.frame(
  start    = 0,
  end      = tau,
  auclast  = TRUE,
  cmax     = TRUE,
  tmax     = TRUE,
  ctrough  = TRUE,
  cstart   = TRUE,
  cav      = TRUE,
  ptr      = TRUE,
  deg.fluc = TRUE,
  swing    = TRUE
)

o_data_ss <- PKNCAdata(o_conc_ss, o_dose_ss, intervals = ss_intervals)
o_nca_ss  <- pk.nca(o_data_ss)

as.data.frame(o_nca_ss) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "ctrough", "cstart", "cav",
                          "ptr", "deg.fluc", "swing")) |>
  select(Subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  arrange(Subject)
```

---

## Parameter reference

### Cstart and Ctrough

`cstart` is the concentration at the **start** of the interval (time = `start`). For steady state this equals the pre-dose trough.
`ctrough` is the concentration at the **end** of the interval (time = `end`). For steady state, `cstart` ≈ `ctrough`.

```{r}
as.data.frame(o_nca_ss) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cstart", "ctrough")) |>
  select(Subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  arrange(Subject, PPTESTCD)
```

### Cav — average concentration

`cav = AUCτ / τ`. Useful for computing clearance at steady state (CL/F = dose / (AUCτ)).

```{r}
as.data.frame(o_nca_ss) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "auclast")) |>
  select(Subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(cav_check = auclast / tau) |>
  arrange(Subject)
```

### PTR, degree of fluctuation, swing

These describe how much concentrations vary within a dosing interval — important for characterizing exposure variability and clinical relevance.

| Parameter | Formula |
|---|---|
| `ptr` | Cmax / Ctrough |
| `deg.fluc` | (Cmax − Cmin) / Cav × 100% |
| `swing` | (Cmax − Cmin) / Cmin × 100% |

```{r}
as.data.frame(o_nca_ss) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("ptr", "deg.fluc", "swing")) |>
  select(Subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  arrange(Subject)
```

### Ceoi — concentration at end of infusion

`ceoi` is the concentration at the end of infusion (time = dose time + `duration`). It is meaningful only for infusion dosing with a nonzero duration; for bolus or oral dosing (duration 0) it is generally not meaningful — it simply returns the concentration at the dose time.

```{r}
# 100 mg infused over 1 h into V = 30 L with CL = 5 L/h (plateau = rate/CL = 20 mg/L)
ke_inf <- 5 / 30
t_inf  <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 12)
c_inf  <- ifelse(t_inf <= 1, 20 * (1 - exp(-ke_inf * t_inf)),
                 20 * (1 - exp(-ke_inf)) * exp(-ke_inf * (t_inf - 1)))
d_inf      <- data.frame(Subject = 1, time = t_inf, conc = round(c_inf, 3))
d_dose_inf <- data.frame(Subject = 1, dose = 100, time = 0, duration = 1)

o_conc_inf <- PKNCAconc(d_inf, conc ~ time | Subject)
o_dose_inf <- PKNCAdose(d_dose_inf, dose ~ time | Subject,
                        route = "intravascular", duration = "duration")
o_nca_inf  <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc_inf, o_dose_inf,
                               intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12,
                                                      ceoi = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)))

as.data.frame(o_nca_inf) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("ceoi", "cmax")) |>
  select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
```

Here `ceoi` equals `cmax` because an infusion peaks exactly when the pump stops. After bolus or oral dosing there is no infusion end, so request `cmax`/`tmax` instead.

## Multiple dosing occasions in one dataset

When data span multiple dose occasions, define one interval row per occasion per group. PKNCA applies each interval independently. For the full interval-specification rules, see the vignette [Selection of Calculation Intervals](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v03-selection-of-calculation-intervals.html).

```{r}
# Two dosing intervals: 0-12h and 12-24h
# Drop the duplicate t=12 row before shifting; PKNCA uses a boundary sample for both adjacent intervals
d_conc_occ1 <- d_conc_ss |> filter(time < 12)   # first interval: 0 to <12
d_conc_occ2 <- d_conc_ss |> mutate(time = time + 12)  # second interval: 12 to 24

d_conc_2dose <- bind_rows(d_conc_occ1, d_conc_occ2)

# Two dose events
d_dose_2dose <- bind_rows(
  d_dose_ss |> mutate(time = 0),
  d_dose_ss |> mutate(time = 12)
)

o_conc_2d <- PKNCAconc(d_conc_2dose, conc ~ time | Subject)
o_dose_2d <- PKNCAdose(d_dose_2dose, dose ~ time | Subject, route = "extravascular")

# One interval per occasion
two_dose_intervals <- data.frame(
  start    = c(0, 12),
  end      = c(12, 24),
  auclast  = TRUE,
  cmax     = TRUE,
  deg.fluc = TRUE
)

o_nca_2d <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc_2d, o_dose_2d, intervals = two_dose_intervals))

as.data.frame(o_nca_2d) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "deg.fluc")) |>
  select(Subject, start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  arrange(Subject, start, PPTESTCD)
```

### Letting PKNCA choose the intervals

Without `intervals`, `PKNCAdata()` generates them from the dose and sample times (≥ 0.13.0). For these two doses it finds the dosing interval from 0 to 12 hours, and the steady-state interval one τ (12 hours) after the last dose:

```{r}
o_data_2d_auto <- PKNCAdata(o_conc_2d, o_dose_2d)

o_data_2d_auto$intervals |>
  filter(Subject == 1) |>
  select(Subject, start, end, impute, aucint.last, cmax, half.life)
```

The generated intervals request the `aucint.*` parameters with `start_cmin` imputation for the dosing interval and `start_predose` imputation at steady state. [Automatic Intervals and Dosing Regimens](auto-intervals.qmd) explains how those choices are made and what happens with missed or late doses and regimen changes.

---

## Finding tau automatically: `find.tau()`

When the dosing interval is not known a priori, `find.tau()` finds it from one subject's dose times. In 0.13.0 it was rebuilt on `find.dose.regimen()` (≥ 0.13.0): the dose times are sorted and duplicates dropped, and then the repeating pattern is found. The result is matched to the usual nominal intervals (every 4 hours to every 12 weeks), so doses recorded a little early or late still give the nominal interval. Times without a unit are taken to be hours; give `timeu` for other units. `find.tau()` returns `0` for a single dose time and `NA` when there are no dose times or no interval repeats. Missed or off-schedule doses still give the underlying interval, with a `pknca_warning_tau_irregular_dosing` warning that names them.

```{r}
# Dose times for one subject: 0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 h
dose_times <- c(0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60)
find.tau(dose_times)

# Recorded a little off schedule, and with the 36 h dose missed
find.tau(c(0, 11.5, 24, 48, 60.5))
```

Detect tau from the two-occasion dataset above:

```{r}
# find.tau() expects one subject's dose times — filter before calling
tau_detected <- find.tau(d_dose_2dose$time[d_dose_2dose$Subject == 1])
cat("Detected tau:", tau_detected, "h\n")
```

The details, including `find.dose.regimen()`, time units, and the `tau.choices` option, are in [Automatic Intervals and Dosing Regimens](auto-intervals.qmd#how-the-dosing-interval-is-found).

## Multiple-dose MRT and Vss {#multiple-dose-mrt-and-vss}

`mrt.md.obs`, `mrt.md.pred`, `vss.md.obs`, and `vss.md.pred` estimate MRT and the volume of distribution at steady state from a steady-state dosing interval:

$$MRT_{md} = \frac{AUMC_\tau + \tau \cdot (AUC_\infty - AUC_\tau)}{AUC_\tau} \qquad V_{ss} = CL \times MRT_{md}$$

The τ·(AUC∞ − AUCτ) term accounts for the drug still in the body at the end of the interval, which AUMCτ/AUCτ alone leaves out.

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mrt.md.obs` | Multiple-dose MRT (AUC∞ extrapolated with observed Clast) |
| `mrt.md.pred` | Multiple-dose MRT (AUC∞ extrapolated with predicted Clast) |
| `vss.md.obs` | Vss from `mrt.md.obs` and `cl.last` |
| `vss.md.pred` | Vss from `mrt.md.pred` and `cl.last` |

These parameters need τ. A `tau` column in the intervals gives it and takes precedence whenever it is present (≥ 0.13.0). Without that column, τ is detected from the group's dose times with `find.tau()`, which needs at least two doses. The steady-state dataset above records only the profiled dose, so nothing repeats and the `tau` column is required:

```{r}
md_intervals <- data.frame(
  start      = 0,
  end        = tau,
  tau        = tau,
  mrt.md.obs = TRUE,
  vss.md.obs = TRUE
)

o_nca_md <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc_ss, o_dose_ss, intervals = md_intervals))

as.data.frame(o_nca_md) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("mrt.md.obs", "cl.last", "vss.md.obs")) |>
  select(Subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  arrange(Subject)
```

For the one-compartment model used in the simulation, MRT is 1/ke + 1/ka ≈ 13.2 h at the typical ke of 0.08/h. The individual estimates spread around that value because ke varies between subjects.

If τ can be neither given nor detected, these parameters are `NA` with a `pknca_warning_tau_undetermined` warning. PKNCA does not fall back to the single-dose equation. For IV infusions, use `mrt.ivmd.obs`, `mrt.ivmd.pred`, `vss.ivmd.obs`, and `vss.ivmd.pred` (≥ 0.13.0). They subtract half the infusion duration, without which MRT is high by `duration/2` and Vss by CL × `duration/2`.

---

## Accumulation ratio

The accumulation ratio compares a steady-state interval with the first dosing interval, for example AUCτ,ss / AUCτ,1. PKNCA calculates it directly as a secondary parameter (≥ 0.13.0): `ratio.auclast`, `ratio.aucint.last`, `ratio.cmax`, and the other `ratio.*` parameters divide a parameter in one interval by the same parameter in a reference interval. `interval_add_secondary()` links the steady-state interval to the first-dose interval. See [Secondary Parameters](secondary-parameters.qmd#ratios) for a worked accumulation-ratio example. To predict accumulation from single-dose data instead, see [Superposition](superposition.qmd).
